events.title: Galileo Arrives in Rome for Inquisition Trial
events.description: Galileo Galilei arrived in Rome to face the Roman Inquisition over his book Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems, which defended the heliocentric model of Copernicus. He was tried later that year and forced to recant.
events.significance: The trial became a landmark episode in the conflict between scientific inquiry and religious authority, and it remains a symbol of the struggle for intellectual freedom.

events.title: Execution of Catherine Howard
events.description: Catherine Howard, the fifth wife of King Henry VIII of England, was beheaded at the Tower of London after being convicted of treason under a Bill of Attainder for adultery.
events.significance: Her fall highlighted the dangers of Tudor court politics and the absolute power of Henry VIII, and it shaped the succession politics that led to his later marriages.

events.title: Bombing of Dresden Begins
events.description: On the night of February 13-14, British and American bomber forces began a massive air raid on the German city of Dresden. Firestorms destroyed much of the historic city center and killed an estimated 25,000 people.
events.significance: The bombing remains one of the most controversial Allied actions of World War II, prompting enduring debate about the morality and military necessity of strategic bombing.

events.title: Budapest Falls to the Soviet Army
events.description: After a siege of about 50 days, Soviet forces took control of Budapest, ending the German and Hungarian defense of the city. The siege caused heavy civilian casualties and extensive destruction.
events.significance: The capture of Budapest opened the way for Soviet advances into Austria and southern Germany and marked a major step toward Soviet domination of Hungary after the war.

events.title: Final Original Peanuts Strip Is Published
events.description: The last original daily-format Peanuts comic strip by Charles M. Schulz was published, and the final Sunday strip ran the following day, shortly after his death on February 12, 2000.
events.significance: It marked the end of one of the most influential and widely read comic strips in history, which ran for nearly 50 years and shaped popular culture worldwide.
